name: Hearthstone Firearms Plinker-22 'Tin Can'
description:
The Hearthstone Plinker-22 is a semi-automatic pistol chambered in .22 LR, built with a zinc-alloy slide and polymer frame that together weigh less than a loaded magazine for most duty pistols. The weapon is sold in the sporting goods section of general retailers alongside fishing rods and camp stoves. It costs less than a quality pair of boots.

The Plinker serves two populations with zero overlap. Recreational shooters in the Mids buy it for target practice and weekend plinking at sanctioned ranges — it is cheap to shoot, fun to use, and mechanically simple enough to teach firearms basics. Shelf residents buy it because it is the second-cheapest gun available and marginally more reliable than the cheapest. In either context, nobody mistakes it for a serious defensive weapon.

Hearthstone makes no pretense about the Plinker's capabilities. Their marketing materials describe it as 'recreational' and 'introductory,' and the packaging includes a prominent disclaimer that the weapon is 'not recommended as a primary personal defense tool.' This disclaimer satisfies Hearthstone's legal department while tacitly acknowledging that many buyers will ignore it entirely.
specifications:
caliber: .22 LR
effective_range: 20 meters
rate_of_fire: Semi-automatic
magazine_capacity: 10 rounds
weight: 0.32 kg
tactical_use: No meaningful tactical application. The .22 LR round from this barrel length is insufficient against any form of body armor and marginal against unarmored targets. In absolute extremis, it is better than nothing. Effective only as a training tool for basic marksmanship fundamentals.
cultural_context: The Tin Can is childhood nostalgia for Mid-district residents who grew up shooting at ranges with their parents. For Shelf residents, it is a grim reminder that even the most basic self-defense comes with a price tag. The weapon occupies completely different emotional spaces depending on who is holding it.
story_hooks: A Shelf teenager with nothing but a Plinker-22 successfully defends their family against armed intruders — the story goes viral and becomes a flashpoint for arguments about arms access and inequality.
Someone is converting Plinker-22s to fire a proprietary micro-cartridge with ten times the standard muzzle energy. The modifications are invisible from the outside.

physical_description.visual_profile: A deliberately diminutive semi-automatic pistol with the proportions of a toy gun — stubby barrel, shallow grip, almost cartoonish in its compactness. The silhouette reads as 'learner's weapon' or 'novelty item' at first glance, not a serious firearm.
physical_description.dimensions: Total length: 16.5 cm | Barrel length: 10.2 cm | Height: 10.8 cm | Width: 2.8 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Featherlight — feels almost insubstantial in the hand, like holding a hardened water bottle. No heft, no authority. A child could manage its recoil.
physical_description.primary_material: Zinc-alloy slide over injection-molded polymer frame — cost-optimized construction visible in every angle
physical_description.finish: Matte zinc with a faint metallic sheen, deliberately non-tactical. The polymer frame has a slightly glossy consumer-grade appearance, like sporting goods store inventory
physical_description.color_scheme: Flat gunmetal gray slide with natural black polymer grip — intentionally boring, bordering on dingy
physical_description.grip_texture: Smooth, slightly waxy polymer with minimal texture — designed for comfort over control, feels like a toy pistol to trained hands
distinctive_features: Comically short barrel with a slightly flared muzzle
Oversized trigger guard suggesting this was designed for gloved or large hands
Simple sights that look almost cosmetic
Exposed blowback mechanism with minimal concealment
Small safety lever that looks incidental rather than integral
Magazine well with generous beveling for easy insertion
Visible wear around ejection port from countless plinking rounds
No rails, no accessory hardpoints — deliberately minimal
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Hearthstone Firearms stamped in thin serif font on the left slide; serial number etched in tiny digits below barrel; 'MADE IN SETTLEMENT LAKES INDUSTRIAL ZONE' on the frame in nearly illegible print
physical_description.condition_typical: Scuffed and worn from casual use — handling marks on the grip, slide scratches from being tossed into range bags, carbon fouling around the chamber from neglectful maintenance. Never well-maintained, but also never abused hard enough to break
